formal_statement: ¬ (∀ (x1 x2 : ℕ),   let x3 : Type := Finset (Finset (Fin x1));   have x4 : Finset (Fin x2) := Finset.univ;   ∀ (x5 : x3) (x6 : Fin x2 → Finset (Fin x1)) (x7 x8 : Fin x2 → x3) (x9 : x3),     have x10 : Fin x1 → Finset (Finset (Fin x1)) := fun (x10 : Fin x1) => {x11 ∈ x5 | x10 ∈ x11};     have x11 : Fin x2 → x3 := fun (x11 : Fin x2) => x7 x11 ∩ x8 x11;     have x12 : Fin x2 → x3 → Prop := fun (x12 : Fin x2) (x13 : x3) => ∀ x14 ∈ x13, (∃ x16 ∈ x6 x12, x14 ∈ x10 x16 ∧ x10 x16 ⊆ x13) ∨ ∃ x16 < x12, x14 ∈ x11 x16 ∧ x11 x16 ⊆ x13;     (∀ (x13 : Fin x2), x12 x13 (x7 x13) ∧ x12 x13 (x8 x13)) →       (∀ x14 ∈ x9, ∃ (x16 : Fin x2), x14 ∈ x11 x16 ∧ x11 x16 ⊆ x9) →         ∃ (x15 : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit x1),           x15.WellFormed ∧             x15.size = x2 ∧               (have x16 : Finset (Fin x15.size) := Finset.univ;                 ∀ (x17 : Fin x1), {x18 ∈ x16 | x17 ∈ x15.leftVars x18 ∨ x17 ∈ x15.rightVars x18}.card ≤ {x18 ∈ x4 | x17 ∈ x6 x18}.card) ∧                 ∀ x16 ∈ x5, x15.eval x16 = Bool.true ↔ x16 ∈ x9)
plain_statement: It is false that: Let T be a family of sets of n variables (tests). Suppose m gates j each have a variable set V_j and test families L_j, R_j (gate family L_j ∩ R_j) such that every member of L_j (and of R_j) lies in a piece inside L_j (R_j), a piece being the tests of T holding one variable of V_j or the family of an earlier gate; and every member of a family S lies in a gate family inside S. Then some well-formed AND-count circuit with exactly m AND gates, each variable bare in at most as many gates as V_j's hold it, is true at a test of T exactly when it lies in S.

counterexample.description: Its literal negation pair, L-meta-7081, is checked (run-058344); recorded by the hub in the same act.
